questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ammonia evolved from the treatment of 0.30 g of an organic compound for the estimation of nitrogen was passed in 100 mL of 0.1 M sulphuric acid. The excess of acid required 20 mL of 0.5 M sodium hydroxide solution for complete neutralization. The percentage nitrogen in the organic compound is
questions.solution:
Equivalents of NH3 evolved

$= \dfrac{1 0 0 \times 0 \cdot 1 \times 2}{1 0 0 0} - \dfrac{2 0 \times 0 \cdot 5}{1 0 0 0} = \dfrac{1}{1 0 0}$

Percent of nitrogen in the unknown organic compound

$= \dfrac{1}{1 0 0} \times \dfrac{1 4}{0.3} \times 1 0 0 = 4 6 . 6$

questions.q: A red solid is insoluble in water. However, it becomes soluble if some $KI$ is added to water. Heating the red solid in a test tube results in liberation of some violet coloured fumes and droplets of a metal appear on the cooler parts of the test tube. The red solid is
questions.solution: $Hg{I}_{2}$ is orange-red in appearance and hardly soluble in water. It dissolves in excess of $I^{-}$ giving complexes $Hg{I}_{3}^{-}$ and $Hg{I}_{4}^{2 -}$. Violet fumes are liberated due to the release of Iodine gas upon heating.

questions.solution: ${H}_{2}S$ in presence of aqueous solution precipitates sulphide of $Cu$ and $Hg$ (IInd group) apart from $\text{P}{\textb^{+ 2}, \text{B}{\texti^{+ 3}, \text{C}{\textd^{+ 2}, \text{A}{\texts^{+ 3}, \text{S}{\textb^{+ 3}$ and $\text{S}{\textn^{+ 2}, \text{M}{\textn^{2 +}, \text{N}{\texti^{2 +}$ are of IVth group so cannot be precipitated by ${H}_{2}S$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution of a metal ion when treated with KI gives a red precipitate which dissolves in excess KI to give a colourless solution. Moreover, the solution of metal ion on treatment with a solution of cobalt (II) thiocyanate gives rise to a deep blue crystalline precipitate. The metal ion is
questions.solution:
When a solution of a $Hg^{2 +}$ is treated with KI a red precipitate of $( Hg{I}_{2} )$ is obtained which dissolves in excess KI to give a colourless solution $( Hg{I}_{4}{)}^{2 -}$. When the solution of $Hg^{2 +}$ is treated with a solution of cobalt (II) thiocyanate a deep blue crystalline precipitate of $Hg ( SCN{)}_{2}$ is formed. The reactions are as follows
$Hg^{2 +} + 2I^{–} \to Hg{I}_{2}$
$\mathop{Hg{I}_{2}}_{( excess )} + 2I^{–} \to \mathop{[ Hg{I}_{4}{]}^{2 –}}_{Soluble}$
${\text{Hg}^{2 +} + \text{Co}{( \text{SCN} )}_{2} \to \mathop{\text{Hg}{( \text{SCN} )}_{2}}_{\text{Blue}\text{crystal}\text{line}\text{ppt}.}$

Here other ion $Pb^{2 +}$ , $Hg^{2 +}$ and $Co^{2 +}$ do not give precipitates formed in these reactions.

questions.solution:
At first $Bi{\left(N{O}_{3}\right)}_{3}$ undergoes hydrolysis.

$2HN{O}_{3} \to {H}_{2}O + 2N{O}_{2} + \left[O\right]$

$2KI + {H}_{2}O + \left[O\right] \to 2KOH + \mathop{I2}_{Darkbrown}$

${I}_{2} + KI \to \mathop{K{I}_{3}}_{yellowsolution}$

options: Nitrogen and sulphur in the organic compound

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 0.45 gm of an organic compound gave on combustion 0.792 gm of CO_{2} and 0.324 gm of water. 0.24 gm of the same substance was Kjeldahlised and the ammonia liberated was absorbed in 50.0 ml of M/8 H_{2}SO_{4}. The excess acid required 77.0 ml of N/10 NaOH for complete neutralisation. Calculate the empirical formula of the compound.
questions.solution:
Calculation of the percentage composition :

i)& Percentage of carbon

$= \dfrac{1 2}{4 4} × \dfrac{{Mass of CO}_{2} \text{Produced}}{\text{Mass of substance taken}} × 1 0 0$

$= \dfrac{1 2}{4 4} × \dfrac{0 \text{.} 7 9 2}{0 \text{.} 4 5} × 1 0 0 = 4 8 \text{.} 0$

ii) Percentage of hydrogen

$= \dfrac{2}{1 8} × \dfrac{{Mass of H}_{2} \text{O produced}}{\text{Mass of substance taken}} × 1 0 0$

$= \dfrac{2}{1 8} × \dfrac{0 \text{.} 3 2 4}{0 \text{.} 4 5} × 1 0 0 = 8 \text{.} 0$

iii) Percentage of nitrogen

mEq. of H2SO4 $= 5 0 × \dfrac{\text{M}}{8} × 2 = 1 2 \text{.} 5$

mEq. of NaOH $= 7 2 × \dfrac{1}{1 0} × 1 = 7 \text{.} 7$

Excess of H2SO4 used to neutralise ammonia

= 12.5 - 7.7 = 4.8

Percentage of N2 $= \dfrac{1 \text{.} 4 × 4 \text{.} 8}{0 \text{.} 2 4} = 2 8 \text{.} 0 \text{%}$

iv) Percentage of oxygen = 100 - (percentage of C + percentage of H + percentage of N) = 100 - (48.0 + 8.0 + 28.0) = 16.0.

b.& Calculation of empirical formula :

&
Element Percentage Atomic mass number of atoms Relative number of atoms Simlpest atomic ratio Simplest whole number atomic ratio
Carbon 48.8 12 $\dfrac{4 8 . 0}{1 2} = 4$ $\dfrac{4}{1} = 4$ 4
Hydrogen 8.0 1 $\dfrac{8 . 0}{1} = 8$ $\dfrac{8 . 0}{1} = 8$ 8
Nitrogen 28.0 14 $\dfrac{2 8 . 0}{1 4} = 2$ $\dfrac{2}{1} = 2$ 2
Oxygen 16.0 16 $\dfrac{1 6 . 0}{1 6} = 1$ $\dfrac{1}{1} = 1$ 1


Hence, the empirical formula of the compound is C4H8N2O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct match between item 'I' and item 'II' is
Item I (Compound) Item II (Reagent)
(1) Lysine (P) 1-naphthol
(2) Furfural (Q) ninhydrin
(3) Isopropyl alcohol (R) ${KMnO}_{4}$
(4) Vinyl benzene (Styrene) (S) Ceric ammonium Nitrate
questions.solution:
Lysine (amino acid) can be tested by ninhydrin as ninhydrin test is used for testing amino acids.
Furfural can be tested by 1-naphthol.
Isopropyl alcohol can be tested by Ceric ammonium nitrate which is a yellow reagent and on reaction with alcohol changes to red.
Vinyl benzene (Styrene) can be tested by $\text{KMn}{\text{O}_{4}$ as styrene decolourises alk. $\text{KMn}{\text{O}_{4}$ due to presence of unsaturation (double bond).
